reason: The issue proposes the fix: cast the arguments to the common type that the bind already computes. The expected types come from the existing TryGetMaxLogicalType, so any such fix passes all three queries.

deciding_assertions: test_window_clause.test: w AS (base [ROWS|RANGE|GROUPS ...]) after base AS (ORDER BY a) gives the v1.5.4 results; forward reference w AS (base), base AS (...) and self reference w AS (w) give 'does not exist'
reason: The issue names v1.5.4 as reference, gives all four inheritance cases and suggests registering each named window as it is transformed. That narrowest fix passes them and still rejects forward and self references with the existing 'does not exist' message.

deciding_assertions: not_in_null.test: EXPLAIN ... WHERE i NOT IN (NULL) AND i > 0 must show Empty Result
reason: The narrowest fix mirrors the existing IN handling and adds a NOT(IN NULL) case to the expression-filter statistics check; it passes the single-predicate case. With an extra conjunct on the same column the scan filter becomes a conjunction, and the existing conjunction check drops FILTER_FALSE_OR_NULL, so that fix fails the AND assertion, which the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: bloom_filters.test: x IS NOT DISTINCT FROM 0.0 / -0.0 on a file with a -0.0 row group must scan 1 / 2 row groups and count 2048
reason: The narrowest fix lets IS NOT DISTINCT FROM use the same Bloom probe as equality; it passes the r = 201 / r IS NOT DISTINCT FROM 201 checks. It hashes only the bit pattern of the constant, so it prunes the -0.0 row group for 0.0 and gives count 0. The signed-zero handling is an equality-probe problem that the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: bloom_filters.test: WHERE list_value[1] IN (101, NULL) must scan 0 / 10 row groups
reason: A reasonable fix routes IN over a nested leaf to the Bloom probe for each constant and bails out on any non-plain constant such as NULL. It passes the issue's list case and the struct variant, but fails the NULL-candidate case, which the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: test_asof_join_setops.test: EXCEPT ALL / INTERSECT ALL as ASOF probe side, build side, both sides, INNER, NLJ predicate, at asof_loop_join_threshold 0 and 32, give the plain join rows
reason: The cause is that set-op planning appends a ROW_NUMBER column to the logical operator types. The natural fix restores those types (or uses the planned children's types) and fixes the join for either side and both ASOF paths. The other-side and join-type cases are direct variants of the stated case.

deciding_assertions: dict_fsst_expression_filter.test: encrypted multi_segment table (50000 rows, vectors span DICT_FSST segments) with split_part(...)::INTEGER % 2 = 0 must give 25000, 624975000
reason: The narrowest fix stops the DICT_FSST filter from evaluating the expression on the unused NULL dictionary slot. It passes the issue's partial_segment and full_vector queries and the >= 10000 variants. The multi-segment fallback case is a separate path that the real fix changes in standard_column_data.cpp. The issue does not mention it, and I could not confirm that the slot fix alone passes it.

deciding_assertions: instr_zonemap_pruning.test: instr(s, 'mmm'|'aaa'|'zzz') = 1 scans 1 / 3; 1 = instr(s, 'mmm') scans 1 / 3; instr(s, 'qqq') = 1 scans 0 / 3
reason: A reasonable fix rewrites instr(s, c) = 1 to the existing prefix(s, c), which already prunes by string stats; it passes the other prefixes and the out-of-range prefix. The flipped equality 1 = instr(...) is the same comparison written the other way; a fix that matches only one side would fail it, so this depends on what counts as a direct variant.

deciding_assertions: natural_join.test: a NATURAL LEFT JOIN b NATURAL JOIN c RIGHT JOIN d ON true gives 1 9
reason: The test is the issue's own query with the expected row the issue gives. Any fix that makes the join chain associate correctly passes it.

deciding_assertions: zero_column_filter_reconstruction.test: duplicate nextval filters give currval 2 (no dedup); leaf/right nextval filters run once before the join; intermediate nextval filter between joins gives count 3 and currval 2
reason: The narrowest fix keeps zero-column filters by extracting them as filters with an empty relation set and placing them above the rebuilt join tree; it passes the WHERE NULL and random() cases. It fails the intermediate volatile test, where the filter must stay between the joins. If it goes through the existing filter_set dedup, it also fails the duplicate nextval test. The issue does not mention the evaluation count or position of volatile filters.

deciding_assertions: histogram_exact(n, [10, 10, 20]) gives {10=0, 20=1, MAX=14} and sums to 15; histogram(n, [10,10,10,10]) gives {10=3, MAX=12} and sums to 15
reason: The issue names the cause exactly: counts is sized from the boundary count before dedup. The narrowest reasonable fix sizes counts after dedup (or keeps the overflow index in sync), which restores the overflow bucket for both histogram and histogram_exact; the expected maps follow from the existing no-duplicate behaviour. It passes every assertion.

deciding_assertions: test_sequence.test: CREATE SEQUENCE ... START NULL / MINVALUE NULL / MAXVALUE NULL / INCREMENT BY NULL must match <REGEX>:.*Parser Error.*START value must not be NULL.* (and MINVALUE/MAXVALUE/INCREMENT variants)
reason: The issue asks for a regular error naming the option and gives as example 'Binder Error: SEQUENCE start value must not be NULL'. A fix that uses that example text (a BinderException, lowercase 'start value') fails the regexes, which need 'Parser Error' and the exact uppercase phrases 'START value', 'MINVALUE', 'MAXVALUE', 'INCREMENT must not be NULL'. The exact messages are chosen by the real fix and the issue does not give them.

deciding_assertions: parquet_filter_narrowing_cast.test: FLOAT 0.1 read as DOUBLE gives correct counts for >, >=, =, <>, IN, <; FLOAT 0.7 for < and >=; two-row file with row group pruning; BIGINT 2 as DOUBLE for > 1.5 and = 1.5; DECIMAL(18,2) 1.25 as DECIMAL(18,3) for > 1.245
reason: All tested cases are the issue's own cases or the operators it lists, and the expected counts are the correct SQL results (the same as with pushdown disabled). The narrowest reasonable fix, the issue's proposal to gate TryCastConstant on CastIsInvertible or an exact round-trip check, passes every assertion.

deciding_assertions: statistics_least_greatest.test: EXPLAIN shows Empty Result for greatest(id,5)<3 and least(id,5)>10 on non-null and nullable columns, and for greatest(a,b)<0 / least(a,b)>2000000 on two nullable columns; no Empty Result when the range overlaps the predicate
reason: The issue asks that least/greatest propagate statistics so the issue's query needs no scan; least is in the title, so it is a direct variant. A normal stats callback that combines child min/max (with any sound treatment of NULL inputs) gives ranges that make all pruned cases empty and keeps the overlapping cases. Only an overly cautious fix that gives up when any input can be NULL would fail the nullable cases; I do not count that as the normal design, but a reader could.

deciding_assertions: statistics_string_length.test: EXPLAIN ANALYZE ... WHERE strlen(v) > 30 and WHERE strlen(v) < 10 on the issue's table show Row Groups Scanned: 1 / 2
reason: The tests are the issue's own two queries. The narrowest reasonable fix adds a statistics callback for strlen from the string length stats, as length() already has, and that gives the row-group pruning the issue expects. It passes both assertions.

deciding_assertions: bloom_filters.test: EXPLAIN ANALYZE ... WHERE r BETWEEN 201 AND 201 and WHERE r >= 201 AND r <= 201 show Row Groups Scanned: 0 / 10
reason: The tests are the issue's two query forms with another absent value on the existing bloom test file. Any reasonable fix (turn equal inclusive bounds into equality in the filter combiner, or let the Parquet reader probe the Bloom filter for a closed range with equal bounds) prunes all row groups and passes.

deciding_assertions: parquet_expression_filter_pruning.test: strlen(s) > 30 on VARCHAR and octet_length(b) > 30 on BLOB show Row Groups Scanned: 1 / 3, with correct counts 2048
reason: The issue asks to derive exact string lengths from Parquet string min/max when min equals max. In the Parquet stats code BLOB and VARCHAR share one branch, so the narrowest reasonable fix (constant or length stats when exact min == max) covers both and passes. The BLOB/octet_length case is a direct variant through a second entry point; a fix limited to VARCHAR would fail it.

deciding_assertions: test_round_integers.test: statement error for round(9223372036854775807::BIGINT, -19); round of HUGEINT +/-170141183460469231731687303715884105724 at -1 gives ...720 and HUGEINT max/min at -1 errors
reason: The issue shows overflow at precision -1 for TINYINT and a wrong sign for BIGINT near its minimum. A reasonable fix that does the arithmetic in a wider type and checks the range passes those and the other types at -1, but keeps the existing early return of 0 when the precision exceeds the cached powers of ten of the input type, so round(BIGINT max, -19) returns 0 instead of an error. The -19 path and the HUGEINT near-limit cases (where no wider type exists) are cases the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: external_file_cache_async_toggle.test: concurrent toggles of enable_external_file_cache during async Parquet scans complete and return 1000000 / 499999500000
reason: The hidden test is the issue's reproduction, word for word, and expects only that the scans finish with the correct sums. Any fix that removes the use-after-free of the shared file handle (shared ownership or locking) passes; no name or message is checked.

deciding_assertions: bloom_filters.test: greatest(r, r) = 201 and least(r, r) = 201 show Row Groups Scanned: 0 / 10; pass-to-pass test_least_greatest.test: greatest/least of two nextval() calls still evaluate both (2 and 3)
reason: The fail-to-pass tests are the issue's two queries with another absent value. The narrowest reasonable fix rewrites least/greatest of identical arguments to the argument, which yields an equality filter and Bloom pruning. The volatile-argument test checks existing behaviour that a reasonable fix must keep (not folding volatile expressions), so it does not make the task unfair.

deciding_assertions: cte_unused_columns.test (fail-to-pass): EXPLAIN of a materialized CTE read twice or three times through UNION ALL with sum(source_key) must not show unused_payload
reason: The issue asks to prune a column from the scan after COUNT(x) becomes COUNT(*). The narrowest reasonable fix reruns unused-column removal after statistics propagation; it passes the count pruning tests of the issue's shape, but cte_unused_columns.test has no COUNT and tests a separate CTE pruning defect with several readers, which the issue does not mention. That fix fails it.

deciding_assertions: test_streaming_window.test: EXPLAIN of first_value OVER (ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND CURRENT ROW) must not show STREAMING_WINDOW; frames fixed at the partition start (ROWS/RANGE/GROUPS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW or UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) must still stream; result rows for moving frames follow SQL semantics
reason: The issue shows a wrong first_value for a moving ROWS frame that only the optimized (streaming) plan produces. The narrowest reasonable fix stops streaming first_value when the frame start is not UNBOUNDED PRECEDING; it passes every NOT-streaming check, every result row, and keeps streaming for the fixed-start frames that streamed before the fix. Only a fix that drops streaming for frames that streamed correctly before, or that extends the streaming executor to moving frames, would fail an EXPLAIN check, and both change behaviour the issue does not ask to change.

deciding_assertions: invoke.test: invoke(lambda x: x::INTEGER, 'abc') -> Conversion Error: Could not convert string 'abc' to INT32; invoke(lambda x: error('boom'), 1) -> Invalid Input Error: boom; invoke(lambda x: x * 2, max BIGINT) -> Out of Range Error: Overflow in multiplication of INT64
reason: The issue gives the exact one-line fix (fun.SetFallible() in InvokeFun::GetFunction) and asks that lambda errors surface as their ordinary messages. That fix passes all three checks; the overflow case is a direct variant (another runtime error in the lambda body) with the normal existing message.

deciding_assertions: test_printf.test: printf('%c', 255), lower(printf(...)), strip_accents(printf(...)) and printf('%c', i) for i in 200..299 must all fail with regex 'Invalid Input Error:.*Invalid UTF8 produced by format string.*'
reason: The issue reports crashes and INTERNAL errors in string functions on printf('%c', 255) output but does not say what the right behaviour is. Reasonable fixes include encoding the code point as UTF-8 like chr(), making the string functions handle invalid UTF-8, or raising an error in printf; only the last passes, and even then only with the exact new message text 'Invalid UTF8 produced by format string', which the issue never gives.

deciding_assertions: string_row_group_pruning.test: v <> 'a' and v IS DISTINCT FROM 'a' must scan 1 / 2 row groups; string_stats_merge.test: v <> repeat('b', 12) must scan 1 / 2
reason: The issue shows only the strict comparison v > 'a' not pruning (and v >= 'b' working). The narrowest reasonable fix makes strict > and < prune at an exact boundary (respecting truncated stats) and passes all > / < / = checks, but it does not add pruning of <> / IS DISTINCT FROM when min = max = constant, so the not-equal checks still scan 2 / 2. The issue's phrase 'not always leveraged for all types of operations' is vague, so a reader could see <> as implied.

deciding_assertions: statistics_contains.test: EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the issue's contains(s, 30 x's) query must show Row Groups Scanned: 1 / 2; count = 122880
reason: The test is exactly the issue's example. The only usable statistic is the max string length (5 for the 'short' group, below the 30-byte needle), so any reasonable fix that adds stats-based pruning for contains through the existing filter-prune callback passes both checks.

deciding_assertions: json_cast.test and variant_duplicate_keys_shredding.test: '{"a":1,"a":2}'::JSON::VARIANT gives (v).a = 2, keys [a], JSON {"a":2}; '{"outer":{"a":1,"b":2,"a":3}}' gives a = 3 with key order [a, b]
reason: The issue says the results are inconsistent and the keys are duplicated, but does not say which duplicate should win (the extraction returned the first value, the JSON round trip the last). A fix that removes duplicates and keeps the first value is equally reasonable and fails every check that expects the last value; a last-wins fix that moves the key to its last position also fails the [a, b] order.

deciding_assertions: variant_comparator.test: min/max of VARIANT 1, 255, 256 give 1 / 256; min(v, 3) / max(v, 3) give [1, 255, 256] / [256, 255, 1]; cross-type numeric VARIANTs give -1 / 10; finalize(min(v) EXPORT_STATE) gives 1 / 256
reason: The issue names the reference ordering (ORDER BY / variant_comparator) and asks that min/max follow it; all expected values follow from that ordering. The min(v, n) form is the same min/max aggregate through another public overload, so I count it as a direct variant; a fix that only patches the single-argument bind would fail it, which is why confidence is medium.

deciding_assertions: test_quantile_disc_double.test: DOUBLE quantile_disc must equal the DECIMAL result and max(1, ceil(n*q)) for n in 1..200 and q in {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99}, in plain, grouped-lateral and correlated plans, for q = -0.9, and for the list form
reason: The issue asks that the DOUBLE path be deterministic and consistent with the exact DECIMAL path; every expected value is that DECIMAL result. The extra n, q, descending and list cases are direct variants (other values and another entry point of the same function). A correct fix that computes ceil(n*q) robustly (snapping, or a decimal conversion at a sensible scale) passes all of them; a fix that only relies on a compiler flag might not, but then it does not meet the issue's stated target.

deciding_assertions: not_conjunction_simplification.test: NOT (i < 400000 OR i > 600000) must scan [1-8] / 9 row groups (NOT(OR) to AND); also NOT (i >= 10 AND i <= 999989) written by hand must scan [12] / 9
reason: The issue asks that NOT BETWEEN be rewritten into a range (OR) query. The narrowest reasonable fix binds or rewrites NOT BETWEEN (or NOT(AND)) into OR of comparisons and passes the NOT BETWEEN checks, but the test also needs the other De Morgan direction, NOT(OR) to AND, which the issue never mentions, and a binder-level NOT BETWEEN fix also fails the hand-written NOT(AND) check.

deciding_assertions: string_expression_filter_pruning.test: the issue's query returns 9 and its EXPLAIN ANALYZE matches "s = 'k00200000'.*Row Groups Scanned: 1 / 3"; a replace with failing constant casts on an empty table returns 0 without an error
reason: The issue's title names the cause (replace is a no-op) and the natural fix is an optimizer rule that rewrites replace(x, c, c) to x; it produces the filter s = 'k00200000' and prunes to 1 / 3. The empty-table check only needs the rule to skip constants that fail to evaluate (the normal TryEvaluateScalar pattern), which keeps existing behaviour. A stats-propagation design would not print s = 'k00200000', so confidence is medium.

deciding_assertions: parquet_hive_null.test: glob of p=%5F_HIVE_DEFAULT_PARTITION__/*.parquet must find 1 file; the lower-case value '__hive_default_partition__' must also be written to p=%5F_hive_default_partition__ and read back as itself
reason: The issue shows a literal '__HIVE_DEFAULT_PARTITION__' value colliding with the NULL directory but gives no escaping scheme. A reasonable fix could escape the whole value, use another encoding, or raise an error; only percent-encoding exactly the first character gives the directory name the glob checks. The case-insensitive collision of a lower-case value is a further case the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: TestScheduleOnePodGroup_SchedulerNameMismatchUpdatesStatus: PodGroup condition PodGroupInitiallyScheduled, Status False, Reason PodGroupReasonSchedulerError, Message = the existing mismatch error text
reason: The issue asks to expose the schedulerName mismatch failure in PodGroup.Status. The narrowest reasonable fix calls the existing updatePodGroupCondition from the failure-before-scheduling path with the existing condition type, the existing SchedulerError reason (the error is passed as an error status, as for pods) and err.Error(); it passes. A fix that picks the Unschedulable reason would fail, so the reason choice is the one doubt.

deciding_assertions: TestCreateIngressValidation: 'foo.com/=svc:http,tls=secret123,garbage' and 'foo.com/=svc:http,tls,garbage' give the existing 'rule ... is invalid and should be in format ...' error
reason: The issue gives the case, the expected existing error text and the fix (end-anchor the regex). The second case is a direct variant. Anchoring the regex passes both and keeps valid rules valid.

deciding_assertions: TestCheckVolumeSatisfyClaim: capacities and requests past int64 are ordered correctly; error text 'requested PV is too small'
reason: The issue gives the exact fix (compare with Quantity.Cmp) and keeps the existing error text. That fix passes every table row.

deciding_assertions: TestObjectAccessors: VersionedAttributes.GetOldObject() returns the converted v1 old object
reason: The issue names the missing method and says it should work like GetObject. Overriding GetOldObject to return the versioned old object, as GetObject does, passes.

deciding_assertions: Test_nodePlugin_Admit: csidriver/pvc/pv not found + authorizer allows -> allowed; + authorizer denies -> authorizer is called and error stays 'error validating audience "foo": ... not found'
reason: The title asks to fall back to the authorizer check when resolving the pod audience fails. The narrowest reasonable fix calls the authorizer on that error, allows on DecisionAllow, and otherwise returns the existing lookup error, which keeps the existing error messages of the existing tests; it passes. A fix that returns the generic 'not authorized' message on denial would change existing behaviour, so it is not a reasonable fix; the issue text is terse, hence medium.

deciding_assertions: TestCanInheritProbeState calls canInheritProbeState(apiContainerStatuses, name, runtimeID); without it the prober test package does not compile (82 of 85 fail-to-pass tests missing before)
reason: The issue describes the container-ID comparison but gives no helper name or signature. A reasonable fix that does the comparison inline or under another name leaves the test package uncompilable and fails all prober tests.

deciding_assertions: TestContainsExplicitLoopback: 127.0.0.1/32 -> true, 127.0.0.2/32 -> false, existing /8, IPv6 and zero-CIDR cases unchanged
reason: The issue states the rule: the CIDR must contain 127.0.0.1, so 127.0.0.1/32 and 127.0.0.0/8 qualify and 127.0.0.2/32 does not. A fix that checks cidr.Contains(127.0.0.1) and keeps the existing IPv6 and catch-all handling passes.

deciding_assertions: validation_test.go calls validateDetectLocalConfiguration(tc.mode, tc.config) with a new two-argument signature (test package missing before); clusterCIDR errors expect the new message 'must be a comma-delimited list of CIDR blocks (...)' with no index; sync period errors expect per-mode paths iptables/ipvs/nftables.syncPeriod
reason: Renaming the paths to the public names, as the issue asks, does not change the function signature, so the test file does not compile. The new clusterCIDR message and the per-backend syncPeriod paths are not in the issue; a fix with field paths like syncPeriod or clusterCIDR[0] fails.

deciding_assertions: TestPersistISCSIRejectsEscapedPluginPath, TestMountDeviceRejectsEscapedPluginPath, TestUnmountDeviceRejectsEscapedPluginPath, TestDiskSetUpRejectsEscapedPluginPath: makePDNameInternal must still produce an escaping path, and the calls must return an error containing 'escapes plugin directory'
reason: The issue offers several fixes: reject in API validation, or sanitize/escape the IQN in makePDNameInternal. A sanitizing fix makes the tests' precondition (path escapes plugin dir) fail, and an API validation fix does not make persistISCSI/MountDevice return an error. The error text 'escapes plugin directory' is also not in the issue.

deciding_assertions: TestEventSeriesSchemasAreAtomic: GetOpenAPIDefinitions entries for core/v1, events.k8s.io/v1 and events.k8s.io/v1beta1 EventSeries have x-kubernetes-map-type=atomic
reason: The issue scopes the change to the core/v1 EventSeries and calls it a single doc-comment addition. The test reads the generated zz_generated.openapi.go, so the issue's own comment-only fix fails unless the agent regenerates or hand-edits generated code (other), and it also checks the two events.k8s.io EventSeries types that the issue does not name (extra-cases).

deciding_assertions: TestQuantityCacheString calls q.CacheString(); the resource test package does not compile without it (1012 fail-to-pass tests missing before)
reason: The issue reports the data race in String/Size but gives no new method. A reasonable fix that makes String non-mutating without adding CacheString leaves the test package uncompilable, so every test fails.

deciding_assertions: TestHandlePodAdditionsTracksCertificatesOnlyForAdmittedPods: with podA rejected by an admit handler and podB admitted, recorder.TrackedPods == [podB.UID]
reason: The issue proposes one fix: move the TrackPod call after the admission check. The narrowest fix moves the call into the admitted branch and passes the assertion. The recording fake for TrackPod is in the test change itself.

deciding_assertions: TestEndpointDNATRules/ipv4_single_endpoint expects exactly "meta l4proto tcp dnat to 10.180.0.1:80"; ipv6_single_endpoint expects "dnat to [fd00:10:180::1]:80"; TestOverallNFTablesRules, TestSyncProxyRulesRepeated and others change every IPv4 single-endpoint rule to the "dnat to ip:port" form
reason: The issue reports only that the IPv6 single-endpoint DNAT rule crashes nft and gives no target syntax. A narrow fix that changes only the IPv6 rule, or that reverts the single-endpoint special case, keeps the IPv4 text "dnat ip addr . port to 10.180.0.1 . 80" and fails the IPv4 assertions; other valid IPv6 syntaxes also fail the exact rule strings.

deciding_assertions: TestSetOptions_Run_Defaults/empty_option_name: Options ["=output"] gives an error that contains "invalid option format"
reason: The issue asks that an empty flag name be rejected but gives no error text. A reasonable fix adds a check with its own message, for example "flag name must not be empty", and fails the errorContains check. Only a fix that reuses the existing format message passes.

deciding_assertions: TestYAMLReaderFinalLineAtBufferBoundary: for final lines of 4095, 4096, 4097, 8192 and 16384 bytes, the second Read returns the full last line (trailing newline trimmed) with no error, and a third Read returns io.EOF
reason: The test is the issue's own reproduction plus other multiples of the buffer size, which are direct variants. Any fix that returns the final line read together with io.EOF passes, and a following io.EOF is the normal reader behaviour.

deciding_assertions: TestOverallNFTablesRules, TestSyncProxyRulesRepeated, TestSyncProxyRulesStartup, TestBadIPs: single-endpoint service chains must contain exactly "meta l4proto tcp dnat ip addr . port to 10.180.0.1 . 80" instead of the numgen map form
reason: The issue reports super-linear sync time and proposes caching state to skip ListAll and diffing on full sync. The tests check only a special-case rule text for single-endpoint services, which the issue never mentions. A fix along the issue's proposals leaves the rule text unchanged and fails all four tests.

deciding_assertions: TestValidateCustomResource/minProperties expects exactly "fieldX: Too few: 0: must have at least 1 item"; TestValidateCustomResource/minItems expects "fieldX: Too few: 1: must have at least 2 items"
reason: The issue asks for a better MinProperties message and only suggests wording like "must have at least 1 field set". A fix with that wording fails the exact message, and the minItems case is not in the issue, so a fix limited to MinProperties fails it too.

deciding_assertions: TestLocalhostNodePortRejectTransition: the restart transaction must contain "flush chain ... localhost-nodeport-reject-tcp", must NOT contain "delete chain ... localhost-nodeport-reject-tcp", must delete the map element before the counter, and the chain must still exist with zero rules afterwards
reason: The issue asks that the localhost NodePort proxy works after a restart with a loopback nodePortAddresses. A reasonable fix deletes the stale reject map element and then deletes the reject chain and counter in the same transaction; it restores the behaviour but fails the assertions that the chain is only flushed and kept. The flush-and-defer cleanup strategy is an internal design choice that the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: TestParseEnv (whole file) calls ParseEnv with three return values (value, found, err); new cases expect "KEY1= 'val1'" to error with "unexpected content after whitespace following '='"; TestMakeEnvironmentVariablesWithFileKeyRef/value_after_whitespace_following_equals_sign expects an error
reason: The issue asks for the optional missing-file case and the empty-value case to work. A reasonable fix (for example a separate lookup or a sentinel error) keeps ParseEnv's two-value signature, so the whole TestParseEnv file does not compile. The tests also change the parsing of "KEY= 'val'" from an empty assignment to an error with a new message, which the issue does not ask for.

deciding_assertions: All reconciler tests: the test file calls reconciler.Run(runCtx) and go reconciler.Run(ctx) with one argument; before the fix Run takes (ctx, stopCh), so the whole package fails to compile (all 62 tests missing before)
reason: The issue describes a test-only fix: stop each reconciler when its subtest returns and create the context per subtest. That fix changes no code outside the test file, so the hidden test file, which needs a new one-argument Run signature, does not compile against it.

deciding_assertions: Test file calls controllervolumetesting.NewCSIDriver and controllervolumetesting.NewCSIPV, helpers that the real fix adds in attachdetach/testing/testvolumespec.go; the whole package fails to compile without them (all 14 tests missing before)
reason: A reasonable fix makes processVolumeAttachments also add VAs whose CSI driver is not attach-required, but it does not add the test helpers NewCSIDriver and NewCSIPV or the csidrivers fake reactors. Without those names the test file does not compile, so every fail-to-pass test fails.

deciding_assertions: pod_test.go TestPodClaims iterates resourceclaim.PodClaims(pod); the new function is missing before the fix, so the whole resourceclaim test package (86 tests) fails to compile
reason: The issue suggests mirroring the dual-location check inside podEvictionTime. That fix makes the devicetainteviction tests pass but adds no PodClaims function, so the resourceclaim test package does not compile and its fail-to-pass tests fail.

deciding_assertions: TestRetryOnConflictPreservesContextErrorWithoutLastError: RetryOnConflict with fn returning context.Canceled must return an error for which errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) holds
reason: The issue gives this exact repro and asks that an error is always returned when the func fails. The narrowest reasonable fix keeps the func's own error when no retriable lastErr was recorded (or when the backoff did not time out), so it returns context.Canceled or a wrap of it and passes. TestRetryOnConflict still passes because the timeout path keeps returning lastErr.

deciding_assertions: TestPodsByCreationTimeTieBreaker: pods with equal CreationTimestamp, names pod-z/pod-a/pod-m and UIDs uid-z/uid-a/uid-m; Less must order them a < m < z
reason: The issue asks for a deterministic order on equal creation times but names no tie-breaker key. The test data make name and UID sort the same way and namespaces are equal, so a tie-breaker in Less by UID, by name, or by namespace/name (ascending) all pass. Only a descending or unusual key would fail. A fix with stable sort at call sites does not give a predictable order, so it does not solve the issue.

deciding_assertions: TestMutationCacheByIndexConcurrentDelete: in client-go tools/cache, mutationCache.ByIndex must return the cached replacement pod when the indexed object is deleted between IndexKeys and GetByKey
reason: The issue only reports a flaky test in the resourceslice controller (TestControllerSyncPool) with no cause, no failure output, and the reporter could not reproduce it. The hidden test checks a race in mutation_cache.go ByIndex, which the issue never points to. A reasonable fix that makes the resourceslice test or controller robust does not touch ByIndex and fails the hidden test.

deciding_assertions: TestProcessNextWorkItem: success gives NumRequeues 0, error gives NumRequeues 1; processNextWorkItem returns true and processes the key once
reason: The issue names the function, shows the inverted check, gives the standard pattern (Forget on success, AddRateLimited on error) and gives the same NumRequeues repro. The narrowest fix flips the condition to err == nil and passes both subtests.

deciding_assertions: TestCPUAccumulatorFreeCPUsSpreadRoundRobin/multiple_sockets expects [0,2,4,6,1,3,5,7,8,10,...] (round-robin per socket); /spread_across_multi-NUMA... expects [0,2,1,3,4,6,5,7]; /partially_allocated_cores expects [0,4,2,6,3,7] (cores ordered by free-CPU count); TestTakeByTopologyWithSpreadPhysicalCPUsPreferredOption expects an exact new 12-CPU set
reason: The issue proposes one fix: round-robin over a.sortAvailableCores() across all cores. That fix interleaves sockets ([0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14,...]) and fails the multiple-sockets and multi-NUMA cases, which need round-robin within each socket. A per-socket fix that orders cores by core ID also fails the partially-allocated case, which needs cores ordered by free-CPU count. The exact orders are design choices that the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: TestParseQuantity/-9223372036854775808 and TestQuantityAccessorBaseline/int64-min-parsed/AsInt64 expect MinInt64 parsed onto the int64 backend with AsInt64 ok; TestParseQuantity rows such as 9223372036854775807.0 and 1000000000000000000.0 still expect the Dec backend (wantAsInt64 nil)
reason: The issue defines the valid range as [-MaxInt64, MaxInt64] and says values outside it should be clamped or rejected. The test needs -2^63 (outside that range) to parse exactly as MinInt64 on the int64 path, so a fix that follows the stated range fails. Also, a general fix that puts all in-range values on the int64 path, including the same values written with '.0', breaks the rows that still expect the Dec backend.

deciding_assertions: TestAddConditionAndDelete calls `rv, err := addConditionAndDeletePod(...)` (new two-value return); all 121 tests of the package are missing before the fix because eviction_test.go does not compile
reason: The issue asks that the eviction Status carry a resource version but names no internal function. The test file calls the unexported addConditionAndDeletePod with a new (string, error) signature. A reasonable fix that gets the deleted pod's RV some other way keeps the old signature, so the test package does not compile and every hidden test fails.

deciding_assertions: TestSyncTerminatingPodKeepsFailedStatusAfterCleanExit: podStatusFn applied exactly 2 times, final phase Failed with reason Evicted; TestGenerateAPIPodStatusKeepsFailedPhase: cached Failed is kept over a clean exit; TestSyncTerminatingPodShutdownCallbackAfterCleanExit: phase Failed
reason: The issue asks for some durable marker and points to the OOM model (a container terminated reason) as the analogy, without choosing a design. A reasonable fix that sets a container terminated reason, or a pod reason with phase Succeeded, fails the assertions that the pod phase stays Failed through the three-way merge. The assertion that the status callback is applied exactly twice is an internal detail that the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: TestPodGroupPostFilter builds podGroupStateData{podsStateData: ...} (new struct field), so the test file does not compile without it (753 tests missing before); testPlugin postfilter cases expect the exact status message `deallocation and deletion of ResourceClaims completed`
reason: The issue only says to add a PodGroupPostFilter method for DRA that keeps current behaviour. The test uses a new internal field podsStateData and a new exact status message, and neither appears in the issue. A reasonable PodGroupPostFilter that stores per-pod state differently, or keeps the old message, fails compilation or the message checks.

deciding_assertions: nodeallocatabledynamicresources_test.go calls new helpers cloneNodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatuses and replaceSpecialClaimNameInStatus and passes a new fourth argument to patchNodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatus; 854 tests are missing before the fix
reason: The issue reports the placeholder claim name in the pod status patch, but it gives no helper names or signatures. The scheduler test file uses two new unexported helpers and a changed signature. A reasonable fix (for example, replacing the name inside PreBind, or only relaxing validation) does not define them, so the package does not compile and all its hidden tests fail.

deciding_assertions: TestFilterWithAttrsAndPrefixFunction_ShardMismatch: when both the label selector and the shard mismatch, apiserver_watch_filtered_events_total must stay unrecorded (label check must run before the shard check); with only a shard mismatch the counter is 1
reason: The issue is a refactor request: simplify cacher.go to use the predicate's Matches logic instead of calling MatchesSharding and MatchesObjectAttributes directly. It says nothing about check order or the shard-filtered metric. Matches checks sharding first, so a refactor that follows the issue keeps shard-first order and records the metric when both mismatch. That fails the new assertion.

deciding_assertions: TestPodGroupMemberPodsOrderingFunc: pod1 vs pod4 (equal priority, attempts, timestamp) gives -1, reversed gives 1; TestQueuedPodGroupInfoOrdering: pod1 before pod4.
reason: The issue names the missing deterministic tie-breaker in PodGroupMemberPodsOrderingFunc. The narrowest reasonable fix adds an ascending tie-break on pod identity (name, namespace/name or UID); pod1/uid1 sorts before pod4/uid4 under each of them, so all deciding assertions pass. A fix that only makes the old test order-independent would fail, but the issue points at the ordering function as the root cause.

deciding_assertions: TestValidateResourceSliceUpdate/invalid-update-touches-stored-device-node-selector-with-two-terms and invalid-update-adds-device-next-to-stored-device-node-selector-with-two-terms: an update that keeps the stored two-term nodeSelector unchanged must still fail with 'must have exactly one node selector term'.
reason: The create-side checks (exact message, path and value copied from the slice-level check the issue quotes, != 1 so the empty case also fails) follow from the issue. But the issue also suggests that update validation ratchet an unchanged old nodeSelector so that unrelated updates are not blocked. A fix that does this per device skips the check when only an attribute changes or a device is added, and fails the two update tests, which require no extra ratcheting.

deciding_assertions: TestQuantityAsApproximateFloat64 rows decQuantity/intQuantity(0, +-500) give 0; TestQuantityAccessorBaseline zero-at-large-scale(-via-dec) AsApproximateFloat64 gives 0.
reason: The issue asks that a zero value give 0 at any scale, matching AsFloat64Slow. The narrowest fix (return 0 when base is 0, or when the quantity is zero, before the Pow10 multiply) passes every row for both the int and the dec paths; negative scales already give 0.

deciding_assertions: TestStaticPodURLHeaderAndKeys calls staticPodURLHeaderAndKeys(headers) and requires sorted canonical keys (X-Api-Key); the whole test file fails to compile without this helper (all 725 tests missing before).
reason: The issue asks only that makePodSourceConfig stop logging header values. The narrowest fix changes the log call (drop the header or log keys inline). It never adds the new helper staticPodURLHeaderAndKeys, so the package test file does not compile and every fail-to-pass test fails.

deciding_assertions: TestFilterUnusableInheritedNameservers calls the new filterUnusableInheritedNameservers(logger, nameservers); it also requires removing zoned global IPv6 and non-IP values. TestGetPodDNSFiltersUnusableInheritedNameservers requires a localhost fallback when all servers are filtered. The test file fails to compile without the helper.
reason: The issue asks to drop scoped fe80::/10 nameservers when the pod does not use host network. A fix that filters inline in parseResolvConf or GetPodDNS never defines filterUnusableInheritedNameservers, so the test package does not compile. The tests also need behaviour that the issue does not state: removal of zoned non-link-local and malformed values, and a fallback to 127.0.0.1 or ::1.

deciding_assertions: TestRollingUpdatePluginSocketFile_distinctInputs calls the new unexported rollingUpdatePluginSocketFile(pluginDir, podUID); the test file fails to compile without it (all 60 tests missing before).
reason: The endpoint-length tests through Start and PluginListener follow from the issue, and any shortening fallback passes them. But the test file calls a helper with an exact name and signature that the issue does not give. A fix that shortens the name inline in Start, or with another helper name, leaves the package uncompilable.

deciding_assertions: TestDescribeNodeResource/node_without_allocatable_resources: rows print 100m (0%) etc.; pod_being_resized_in_place: row '500m (50%)' and totals 'cpu 500m (50%)'.
reason: Part 1 asks for 0% when allocatable is zero, like the totals. Part 2 asks that rows and totals use the same accounting, and says the rows moved to status resources 'without the totals following'. So the narrowest fix guards the per-pod division and adds UseStatusResources to getPodsTotalRequestsAndLimits, which passes both. Moving the rows back to spec would undo the intended change of #137683.

deciding_assertions: TestUpdatePodGroupRecreatedWithDifferentParent: after the update the old parent no longer lists pg1 and the new parent does; TestRecreatedPodGroupQueueingHints: exactly two hints, Delete(old, nil) then Add(nil, new), for PodGroup and CompositePodGroup.
reason: The issue gives the fix sketch: on a UID change, call deletePodGroup(old) and addPodGroup(new) and return, and do the same for CompositePodGroup. That fix passes both tests through the existing delete and add handlers. No new name or exact value is needed.

deciding_assertions: initializer_test: TestWantsAuthorizer needs initializer.WantsAuthorizer with SetAuthorizer(authorizer.Authorizer) to be called by Initialize; TestWantsUnconditionalAuthorizer keeps the old path. The other tests fail before only because the test file does not compile without WantsAuthorizer.
reason: The issue gives the name WantsAuthorizer and the method SetAuthorizer with authorizer.Authorizer, next to WantsUnconditionalAuthorizer. The narrowest fix adds the interface and calls it in Initialize. This needs the stored authorizer to be an authorizer.Authorizer (change the field and New, or use a type assertion), and the test passes a full Authorizer. All other names used by the tests exist already.

deciding_assertions: names_test.go calls the new GenerateWorkloadName(ownerName, uid) and GeneratePodGroupName(workloadName, templateName); it requires 'job-647cf7d9' and, for an empty owner name, exactly '647cf7d9'.
reason: The issue proposes moving 'a general version' of the Job helpers into the workloadbuilder library but gives no exported names or signatures. A fix that uses other names (for example ComputeWorkloadName) leaves the test package uncompilable. The empty-owner output without a leading dash is also a design choice that the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: Declarative validation tests 'valid priority above user-defined maximum' (HighestUserDefinablePriority+1 with no system class gives no error) for PodGroup, CompositePodGroup and Workload; the generated coverage tables no longer list a 'maximum' origin for priority.
reason: The issue asks to keep the user-defined cap for non-system classes and to relax it to match PriorityClass validation.
